newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 17.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Jan 17.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Telecommunications experts have suggested the Government could receive a lower price for the one-third sale of Telstra, following the company's decision to abandon plans to develop a full service network (FSN), which would allow voice telephony, interactive data and pay TV services to be distributed over a single cable system. The overhaul of the network would have cut Telstra's operating costs by more than A$500 million a year. Page 1.

Since experiencing rapid growth in the last decade, human resources departments are now being forced to downsize, with many already beginning to outsource and automate parts of themselves. While Westpac has 450 human resources employees and Boral has only about 50, Lend Lease has no one specifically working in the area and is attempting to move the responsibility for human resources to the business managers. Page 1.

With recruitment normally slow through January and beginning to pick up by February, Recruitment Solutions executive director Greg Savage says this year there has been an earlier than usual lift in demand for white-collar workers, middle-management and prfessionals. In particular, recruitment is more active in the banking and finance sector, but information technology and sales and marketing are also picking up, according to Hamilton James & Bruce's Peter Ryan. Page 3.

Hoping to establish the city of Gladstone as a global player in the light-weight metals industry, the Queensland Government has asked Italian group Teksid SpA to establish a magnesium metals die-casting plant alongside Queensland Metals Corp Ltd's propose A$700 million smelter. Page 37.

Queensland Metals Corporation managing director Creagh O'Connor said yesterday the 90,000 tonne-a-year commercial smelter at Gladstone would produce 25 per cent of the world's current magnesium metal production if it came on stream today, however the QMC/Normandy project's output is expected to double from 300,000 to 600,000 tonnes a year by the time it comes on stream in 2004. Page 37.

Although Placer Dome Inc now has more than 50 per cent of Highlands Gold Ltd shares, Highlands managing director Ian Goddard said last night that talks with potential underwriters to its plan to spin off its non-Porgera assets were continuing, as the board believes Placer's A$423 million takeover offer significantly undervalues the company. Page 38.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Mining giants RTZ-CRA and BHP have conducted initial discussions which may see a revived second Australian option for the development of a proposed A$3 billion alumina refinery by Comalco Ltd in Queensland. The talks are believed to be centred around Comalco - owned by RTZ-CRA - using BHP's coal seam gas from a nearby mine as an alternative energy source for the massive project. Page 19.

BHP has been granted a waiver from the Australian Stock Exchange for the second time, releasing the mining giant from an obligation to report recent drilling results in domestic waters. BHP has argued the Bass Strait drilling information is seen as a valuble trade secret which could be commercially harmful if results were released prematurely. Page 19.

Singaporean property group Tuan Sing Holdings Ltd as bought a 39 per cent majority stake in the Grand Hotel Group Ltd for A$80.7 million, with the A$2.05 a share purchase price representing a 14.5 per cent premium on GHG's closing price yesterday of A$1.7. The deal has already been approved by the Foreign Investment Review Board. Page 19.

ANZ Bank yesterday announced a series of fee changes which would have been pounced on by the Prices Surveillance Authority two years ago, but will go unchallenged today. The changes will see customers who stick to the old ways of savings books and bank branchs charged more than those who use the new technology of ATMs, telephone banking and the Internet. Page 19.

A consortium which includes the likes of Ford Motor Co and Queensland Metals Corp has committed A$70 million to build a pilot magnesium refinery in the Queensland town of Gladstone. The project acts as a precursor to a planned A$700 million smelter which ill produce up to 30 per cent of the world's magnesium output. Page 21.

Another domestic long-distance telephone carrier is set to begin operation next month following an agreement between AAP Telecommunications and international service provider Telegroup Inc. AAPT - Australia's third largest long-distance phone group - evenually plans a 30 to 60 per cent discount on current rates for international calls through callback services. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In a move which could cost Melbourne's Crown Casino group up to A$280 million, Crown Ltd is considering buying the managing contract from Lloyd Williams' Hudson Conway. Rumours of the possible buyout have surfaced following the group raising A$81.9 million through issuing new shares in December. Page 21.

Normandy Mining is to inject A$20 million into a Queensland magnesium project which could lead to a A$700 million development which will see the Ford Motor Company take out 47 per cent of output from a processing facility to be built at Gladstone under a eal announced yesterday. Page 21.

The Grand Hotel Group, which owns half of Melbourne's Hyatt Hotel and Perth's Hyatt Centre, has lifted its sharemarket prospects by securing Singapore property group, Tuan Sing Holdings, as an investor in the 39 per cent stake bought by ING Barings, salvaging last year's poor float of the hotel property owner. The deal is said to be worth approximately A$80.7 million. Page 21.

Moving away from low interest rates, investors are pouring a record amount of money into managed funds which have the attraction of high returns from a strong sharemarket. GIO Australia's personal investment service has seen sales for the first six monthsto December jump 88 per cent to A$315.3 million. Other funds have reported similar increases, with one fund saying demand was so strong over December, offices were kept open until 9 pm Christmas Eve. Page 21.

Regional pay TV group Austar has been forced to postpone a planned capital raising of A$312 million in the United States because of poor market conditions. Austar planned to use the funds for a A$400 million infrastructure investment in Australia but now he company may be forced to strike a deal with one of the other major Australian pay TV operators. Page 23.

Aussie Home Loans, a non-banking home loan group, reported A$345 million in home lending for November - a 60 per cent increase - despite the big banks' recent attack on the small lenders' cheap loans market. Aussie now ranks as Australia's fifth biggest hme lender with A$4.5 billion in loans written. Page 25.
THE AGE

Signing a contract to buy up to 45,000 tonnes of magnesium a year for 10 years for its worldwide use, Ford Australia yesterday announced an A$700 million project to build the world's biggest magnesium smelting industry. A joint venture between QueenslandMetals Corporation and Normandy Mining will spend about A$40 million on a demonstration plant and another A$30 million on a feasibility study before committing to start construction on the A$700 million smelter in 1999. Page C1.

ING Barings has sold McIntosh Securities' 39 per cent stake in the Grand Hotel Group to a listed Singaporean property group, Tuan Sing, at A$2.05 per security, representing a total purchase price of about A$80.7 million. The sale releases McIntosh from aA$17 million indemnity to ING Barings if the stock had continued to perform poorly. Page C1.

In a bid to move customers from branch banking to electronic services, ANZ Bank yesterday unveiled new fees at the launch of its telephone banking system. The fees offer incentives to use automated teller machines, Eftpos and telephone banking and will hlp the ANZ cut costs to improve its performance. Page C1.

Victorian Democrats Senator Lyn Allison yesterday criticised pay rises at the Australian Taxation Office, recorded in the commissioner of taxation's annual report. The report shows that while the Tax Office was shedding staff, the number of its senior excutives receiving at least A$100,000 increased fivefold in 1995-96. Page C2.

The A$10 million float of the Ballarat-based Golden Hills Mining NL offers a gross cashflow of about A$16 million over three years from the company's Gidginbung heap-leach gold project near Temora in New South Wales and about A$3.8 million in cash. The goup's resource base on listing will be 122,000 ounces of gold, of which 57,700 ounces is estimated for the Mount Egerton gold project near Ballarat. Page C2.

Optus Vision's New South Wales director, Rob Hines, admitted yesterday that the company had failed to meet its targets for delivering local telephony on its high-capacity cable as the hybrid fibre coaxial cable used for the pay TV network had proved to bemore technically difficult to adapt for telephony than expected. Page C2.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
